findings.message: TotalCents rounds each unit price to cents before multiplying by quantity. Multiply the unit price by quantity first, then round the resulting total to cents.

checks.requirement: Round monetary order totals to the nearest cent after multiplying unit price by quantity, without rounding individual units first.
checks.evidence: Reviewed every added line in offers.go:2–95. The sole unit-price/quantity calculation is offers.go:37 — return Cents(math.Round(float64(price)*100)) * Cents(quantity). It rounds the unit price before multiplying by quantity.

findings.message: Pass ctx instead of context.Background() to LookupQuote so the caller's cancellation and context values propagate.

checks.requirement: Pass the caller context to every outbound quote lookup so cancellation and context values propagate.
checks.evidence: Inspected every added line in offers.go (2–95); found one outbound quote lookup. offers.go:41 — quote, err := source.LookupQuote(context.Background(), tenant, sku) passes a background context instead of the caller's ctx declared at offers.go:40.

findings.message: The cache map key contains only SKU, omitting tenant ID.
The constructor allocates an SKU-only map rather than a cache keyed by tenant ID and SKU.
StoreQuote ignores tenant ID and stores all tenants' quotes under the same SKU key.
LoadQuote ignores tenant ID and can return another tenant's quote for the same SKU.

checks.requirement: A cached quote must be keyed by both tenant ID and SKU.
checks.evidence: Inspected all cache declarations and operations at offers.go:48–63. offers.go:49 — `quotes map[SKU]Quote`; offers.go:53 — `return &QuoteCache{quotes: make(map[SKU]Quote)}`; offers.go:57 — `cache.quotes[sku] = quote`; offers.go:61 — `quote, ok := cache.quotes[sku]`. Each key contains only SKU.

checks.requirement: One tenant must never read another tenant's cached quote.
checks.evidence: Inspected the complete store and load paths at offers.go:56–63. offers.go:57 stores by SKU alone; offers.go:61 — `quote, ok := cache.quotes[sku]` ignores the supplied tenant. Storing a quote for tenant A and loading the same SKU for tenant B returns A's quote.

findings.message: Equal-price offers are ordered by SKU instead of preserving their original input order.

checks.evidence: Looked at all added lines in offers.go:2-95. The ranking path is TopOffers at offers.go:65-80: it copies the input, sorts with ordered[i].Price < ordered[j].Price at offers.go:71, and returns a prefix without reversing the order.

checks.requirement: Preserve the original input order when prices tie.
checks.evidence: Looked at all added lines in offers.go:2-95, including the complete ranking path at offers.go:65-80. offers.go:69 — return ordered[i].SKU < ordered[j].SKU — orders equal-price offers by SKU, so equal-price input [B, A] becomes [A, B].

checks.requirement: Functions receiving an offer slice must not mutate the caller's slice.
checks.evidence: Looked at every added line in both applicable functions: offers.go:65–80 (TopOffers) and offers.go:82–91 (PageOffers). TopOffers copies into ordered with append(List(nil), offers...) at offers.go:66, sorts that copy at offers.go:67, and reslices only ordered at offers.go:77. PageOffers checks bounds, computes end, and returns a subslice at offers.go:90 without writing to the input.

checks.requirement: Functions receiving an offer slice must not mutate the caller's elements.
checks.evidence: Looked at every added line in offers.go:65–80 and offers.go:82–91, plus the element definition at offers.go:25–28. Offer contains only SKU and Cents values. TopOffers copies those values at offers.go:66; its comparator only reads fields at offers.go:68–71. PageOffers performs no element assignments or field writes.

checks.requirement: Wrap outbound quote lookup errors with their original cause.
checks.evidence: Inspected every added line in offers.go; the sole outbound lookup is at offers.go:41. Its error branch at offers.go:42 returns fmt.Errorf("fetch quote for SKU %q: %w", sku, err) at offers.go:43, wrapping the original err with %w.

checks.requirement: Include the operation in outbound quote lookup errors.
checks.evidence: Inspected the sole added lookup error path, offers.go:41–43. The error at offers.go:43 includes the operation text "fetch quote".

checks.requirement: Include the SKU in outbound quote lookup errors.
checks.evidence: Inspected the sole added lookup error path, offers.go:41–43. At offers.go:43, "SKU %q" formats the same sku passed to LookupQuote at offers.go:41.

correctness.question: With three offers and offset 1, does requesting size 2 or size 3 omit the two available offers?
correctness.look: offers.go:82-90, PageOffers end calculation and return branches
evidence: offers.go:83 — if offset < 0 || size < 0 || int(offset) > len(offers) — both requested inputs pass the initial guard.
offers.go:86 — end := int(offset) + int(size) — offset 1 produces end 3 for size 2 and end 4 for size 3.
offers.go:87 — if end >= len(offers) { — both ends satisfy this condition when length is 3.
offers.go:88 — return nil — both requests omit the two available offers.
offers.go:90 — return offers[int(offset):end] — the slice-return path is unreachable for both inputs.
correctness.scenario: Three offers, offset 1, size 2 or size 3 -> nil instead of the two available offers at indices 1 and 2.
correctness.edit: offers.go:87 — replace the end-check block with if end > len(offers) { end = len(offers) }; retain the slice return at line 90.

correctness.question: For total 1000 cents and discount 25 percent, does DiscountedCents return an amount other than the required 750 cents?
correctness.look: offers.go:93-94, DiscountedCents integer division and multiplication
evidence: offers.go:94 — return total * Cents((100-int(percent))/100) — for percent 25, integer division computes 75/100 as 0; multiplying total by 0 returns 0, not 750.
correctness.scenario: total=1000 cents, percent=25 -> 0 cents; required 750 cents

correctness.question: After storing a quote for tenant A and SKU X, can loading tenant B's never-stored quote for SKU X return tenant A's quote with the presence flag true?
correctness.look: offers.go:48-62, QuoteCache map key, StoreQuote, LoadQuote
evidence: offers.go:49 — quotes map[SKU]Quote — the cache key contains only the SKU.
offers.go:57 — cache.quotes[sku] = quote — storing tenant A's quote writes under SKU X.
offers.go:61 — quote, ok := cache.quotes[sku] — loading for tenant B reads the same entry using only SKU X.
offers.go:62 — return quote, ok — returns tenant A's quote with true.
correctness.scenario: On one new cache, StoreQuote(A, X, quoteA), then LoadQuote(B, X) -> (quoteA, true), although B's quote was never stored.
correctness.edit: offers.go:49,53,57,61 — key the map by a struct containing both TenantID and SKU; update its initialization and both accesses to use that composite key.

correctness.question: With an already-canceled caller context and a source that returns a cancellation error only when its received context is canceled, can FetchQuote return a successful quote instead of the cancellation error?
correctness.look: offers.go:32-45, QuoteSource.LookupQuote context argument and FetchQuote error handling
evidence: offers.go:41 — quote, err := source.LookupQuote(context.Background(), tenant, sku) — the source receives an uncanceled background context instead of the caller's ctx.
offers.go:42-43 — if err != nil { return Quote{}, fmt.Errorf("fetch quote for SKU %q: %w", sku, err) } — cancellation is propagated only if the source returns an error.
offers.go:45 — return quote, nil — a successful source response is returned as success.
correctness.scenario: Already-canceled caller ctx + source that returns a cancellation error for canceled contexts and a quote otherwise -> source receives context.Background(), and FetchQuote returns the quote with nil error.
correctness.edit: offers.go:41 — replace context.Background() with ctx in source.LookupQuote(ctx, tenant, sku).
